data.name: About_Description
data.value: PadForge turns any input device into any virtual controller. Gamepads, joysticks, keyboards, mice, and touchscreens are mapped to virtual game controllers (Xbox, PlayStation, flight sticks, wheels, third-party gamepads) or keyboard+mouse / MIDI output that games treat as real hardware. Powered by HIDMaestro and Windows MIDI Services. It uses SDL3 for controller input, Windows Raw Input for keyboard and mouse, HidHide for per-game device masking, and provides a modern Fluent Design interface for mapping, deadzones, sensitivity curves, and force feedback.

The four sliders below only cap the cardinal axes. Use them to limit range on purpose, not to correct it.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Tooltip
data.value: Reference variables as a, b, c, … (or s[0], s[1], …). Supports + - * / && || ?: and abs/min/max/clamp/sign/lerp. The macro fires on the rising edge when the formula's value crosses 0.5.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Hint
data.value: Each row defines one variable letter (a, b, c, …). Choose Input Device to bind a button, POV, or axis on a physical device, or Output Controller to read a channel on the slot's combined virtual controller output.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_Single_Tooltip
data.value: Fire when variable a goes from 0 to 1.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_Both_Tooltip
data.value: Fire only when both a AND b are active. Classic chord.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_Either_Tooltip
data.value: Fire when either a OR b is active.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_AButNotB_Tooltip
data.value: Fire when a is active and b is NOT active.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_AxisOverHalf_Tooltip
data.value: Fire when stick axis a is deflected more than 50% from rest.

data.name: Macro_AlwaysDesc
data.value: Runs continuously while this virtual controller is active. No trigger button required.

data.name: Macro_KeyComboHint
data.value: Select a key to add it. Example: {Control}{Alt}{Delete}

data.name: Macro_ProcessTooltip
data.value: Process name without .exe. Dropdown shows processes with active audio sessions.

data.name: MacroAction_LightbarColor_Tooltip
data.value: Override the assigned PlayStation slot's lightbar to a chosen RGB color. Reactive fades from full intensity to black over the configured decay window, then hands back to the Lighting tab's settings. Sticky holds the color until a Clear Lightbar Override action runs. Game-driven writes still take priority over the override.

data.name: MacroAction_LightbarColorClear_Tooltip
data.value: Releases any active lightbar override on the assigned slot. Pair with a Sticky Set Lightbar Color action to undo it via another macro.

data.name: MacroAction_LightbarModeSet_Tooltip
data.value: Sets the assigned slot's lightbar mode to a specific value. Persists like a Lighting tab edit until another action or the user changes it.

data.name: MacroAction_LightbarModeCycle_Tooltip
data.value: Advances the slot's lightbar mode through the modes selected below. Each fire moves to the next checked mode. The cycle position is per-action and resets on app restart.

data.name: Macro_LightbarPalette_Empty
data.value: Empty palette uses the slot's own Lighting tab palette.

data.name: Macro_LightbarCycleModes_Hint
data.value: Pick which lightbar modes the macro should cycle through. Each fire advances to the next checked mode.

data.name: MacroAction_Rumble_Tooltip
data.value: Drives the slot's physical device rumble from a macro. Reactive runs at full strength for the hold window then fades to zero across the fade window. Sticky holds at full strength until a Stop Rumble action runs. Layers on top of game-driven rumble via max() so user-driven feedback is always felt.

data.name: MacroAction_RumbleStop_Tooltip
data.value: Releases any active rumble override on the assigned slot. Pair with a Sticky Rumble action to undo the hold via another macro.

data.name: MacroAction_RumbleTrigger_Tooltip
data.value: Drives the slot's trigger vibration from a macro. Same hold modes as Rumble Override, but the strength feeds the trigger channel (Xbox impulse triggers and DualSense Adaptive Trigger Vibration) instead of the grip motors. Max-combines with the trigger routing.

data.name: MacroAction_RumbleTriggerStop_Tooltip
data.value: Releases any active macro trigger vibration on the slot. Pair with a Sticky Rumble Trigger Override to end the hold from a macro.

data.name: Macro_SetGyroEngaged_Tooltip
data.value: Sets the slot's gyro engage state from a macro. Toggle flips the current state. On forces gyro engaged. Off forces it disengaged. Independent of the Gyro tab's engage button. The two sources OR-combine, so neither can disable what the other engaged.

data.name: MacroAction_MouseRecenter_Tooltip
data.value: Snaps the desktop cursor to the center of the primary monitor when this macro fires. Pick which axes recenter.

data.name: MacroAction_MouseFixPosition_Tooltip
data.value: Toggles a sticky cursor pin on press. Press once to pin the cursor at the target coordinate, press again to release.

data.name: MacroAction_MouseLimitRegion_Tooltip
data.value: Toggles a cursor region clamp on press. Press once to keep the cursor inside the region, press again to release.

data.name: MacroAction_MoveMouseToScreenPosition_Tooltip
data.value: Warps the desktop cursor to a fixed screen position on press. Use Pick on screen to capture a spot with the cursor.

data.name: MacroAction_RepeatKeyWhileHeld_Tooltip
data.value: Fires the key on a fixed interval for as long as the trigger is held (autofire / turbo).

data.name: Macro_PickOnScreen_Tooltip
data.value: Click, then move the cursor onto the target. Its position is captured after a short countdown.

data.name: Macro_CursorWrite_Caveat
data.value: While this is active, PadForge writes the cursor position every frame. Games that move the cursor themselves can interfere.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Subtitle
data.value: Per-touchpad input. Gestures (swipes, taps, pinches, shapes) and continuous output modes (virtual stick / D-pad, mouse) become mapping sources you can bind on the Mappings tab.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_GesturesEnabled_Tooltip
data.value: Master toggle for this touchpad. When off, no gesture descriptors fire for this touchpad. Existing finger / click / position mappings still work.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Mode_Tooltip
data.value: Which gesture catalog the engine evaluates against the live finger paths. "Both" is the default.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_CooldownMs_Tooltip
data.value: After a gesture fires, ignore new gestures on this touchpad for this many milliseconds. Prevents bounce-fires from rapid back-and-forth motion.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_RadialZones_Tooltip
data.value: Slide outward from your finger's landing point into a wedge. Zone 0 anchors at the top and zones increase clockwise. Each zone's entry in the picker shows its direction in parentheses as degrees from the top: (0°) is up, (90°) is right, (180°) is down, (270°) is left. Only one zone is held at a time. Sliding into another releases the previous one, so you can cycle through zones in a single swipe.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_TouchSpots_Tooltip
data.value: Held buttons for where the touchpad is touched. One finger lands in Left, Right, or Top (the top quarter). Two or more fingers hold Multitouch. The left/right split sits at two fifths of the width, matching DS4Windows, and exactly one spot is held at a time.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_SectionGated_Hint
data.value: Off until enabled: turn on “Enable Gestures on This Touchpad” under Gesture Detection (and set Recognize to include this catalog). Only then do these appear in the mapping and macro lists.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_ShapeGestures
data.value: Shape Gestures (Circle, Square, Triangle, Z, Checkmark)

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Custom_Empty
data.value: No custom gestures recorded for this profile. Click Record New Gesture to capture one.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Stick_Subtitle
data.value: Turn the touchpad into a virtual analog stick or D-pad. The output anchors where your finger first lands. Current position relative to that anchor drives the stick value and (optionally) latched D-pad direction bools.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_StickEnabled_Tooltip
data.value: Surfaces Touchpad Stick X, Stick Y, and D-Pad descriptors in the mapping picker. Works alongside the existing touchpad-finger and touchpad-gesture sources, not instead of them.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_StickDPadMode_Tooltip
data.value: Off skips D-pad output. 4-Way emits one cardinal at a time. 8-Way emits two cardinals for diagonals (the same way physical D-pads report NE / NW / SE / SW).

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Mouse_Subtitle
data.value: Tunes cursor speed when a touchpad finger is mapped to mouse X/Y on a Keyboard / Mouse virtual controller. 1.0 is the default. Raise either axis for a faster cursor, lower for slower. Invert flips either axis.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseSensitivityX_Tooltip
data.value: Multiplier on horizontal touchpad → mouse delta. Below 1.0 slows the cursor. Above 1.0 speeds it up.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseSensitivityY_Tooltip
data.value: Multiplier on vertical touchpad → mouse delta.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseInvertX_Tooltip
data.value: Flip horizontal motion. Finger right moves the cursor left.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseInvertY_Tooltip
data.value: Flip vertical motion. Finger down moves the cursor up.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Pointer_Subtitle
data.value: Tunes the Touchpad Pointer X/Y sources, which warp the cursor to your finger's position on the pad (map them to mouse X/Y on a Keyboard / Mouse virtual controller). At 1.0 the pad maps 1:1 to the screen. Raise the stretch to reach the screen edges before your thumb reaches the pad edge.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_PointerStretchX_Tooltip
data.value: Horizontal margin stretch around the pad center. 1.5 reaches the screen edges at two thirds of the physical travel.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_PointerStretchY_Tooltip
data.value: Vertical margin stretch around the pad center.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_SwipeHaptics_Subtitle
data.value: Pulses the controller's haptics as your finger travels across this touchpad, like Steam Input's trackpad ticks. Steam Controllers and the Steam Deck tick the actuator under the pad; DualSense and DualShock 4 pulse the rumble motors.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_SwipeHapticsEnabled_Tooltip
data.value: Fires a short haptic tick each time the finger moves a set distance on this pad. Landing a finger or clicking the pad never ticks. Off by default.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_SwipeHapticsIntensity_Tooltip
data.value: Strength of each tick. Game rumble always wins when it is stronger.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_SyntheticPressure_Subtitle
data.value: Simulates DualShock 2 / DualShock 3 pressure buttons on pads that report a touch as full pressure (DualShock 4, DualSense, Steam Controller 2015). While enabled, this device's Pressure mapping sources read no touch as 0%, a resting touch as the Touch Pressure Level, and a pad click as 100%.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_SyntheticPressureEnabled_Tooltip
data.value: Shapes this device's Pressure mapping sources into three steps: no touch reads 0%, a resting touch reads the Touch Pressure Level, and clicking the pad reads 100%. Off by default, which keeps raw readings on pads with true analog pressure.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_SyntheticTouchLevel_Tooltip
data.value: How much pressure a resting (unclicked) touch reports. 50% leaves an even step up to a full pad click.

data.name: Pad_ResetTouchpadTaps
data.value: Reset Tap / Double Tap / Triple Tap

data.name: Recorder_Subtitle
data.value: Draw the gesture on the surface below. The dialog captures every finger you put down. When you take all fingers off the surface the sample is recorded. Drawing a different finger count from previous samples resets the stack.

data.name: Recorder_Waiting
data.value: Waiting for finger contact on the canvas

data.name: Recorder_Waiting_Device
data.value: Draw on the touchpad. The canvas mirrors it live.

data.name: Recorder_TargetDevice_None
data.value: Touchpad unavailable. Use the canvas below with mouse or touch.

data.name: Recorder_Complete
data.value: All samples captured. Name the gesture and click Save.

data.name: Recorder_SampleCount_Hint
data.value: 3 is the standard. More samples = sturdier match, fewer = faster recording.

data.name: Recorder_Error_NoEngine
data.value: Engine not running. Start the engine before recording.

data.name: Recorder_Error_BadSample
data.value: No valid sample captured. Try drawing the gesture again.

data.name: Settings_GyroCalibrate_Tooltip
data.value: Place the controller on a flat surface and click Calibrate Gyro to sample the at-rest reading for ~1.5 seconds. Subtracted from raw readings so gyro mappings don't drift the mouse / stick when the controller is still.

data.name: Settings_GyroResetCalibration_Tooltip
data.value: Clears the at-rest gyro bias and the last-calibrated timestamp. The next polling cycle re-runs the 1.5-second auto-calibration on this device.

data.name: Settings_GyroSensitivityH_Tooltip
data.value: Scales the horizontal (Yaw + Roll) gyro contribution to the output. 1.0 leaves the rate as the engine sees it. Higher values amplify, lower values attenuate. Apply at the device level so every gyro binding on this controller inherits the same horizontal feel.

data.name: Settings_GyroSensitivityV_Tooltip
data.value: Scales the vertical (Pitch) gyro contribution to the output. Separate from horizontal so you can tune aim X and Y independently.

data.name: Settings_GyroDeadZone_Tooltip
data.value: Minimum rotation rate (degrees per second) below which gyro output is treated as zero. Rejects at-rest hand tremor without snapping behavior. Rates past the threshold pass through with the threshold subtracted.

data.name: Settings_GyroAcceleration_Tooltip
data.value: Rate-dependent gain. 0 = off (linear scaling). Higher values let slow movements pass through unchanged while amplifying fast movements. Useful for combining precision aim with quick turns.

data.name: Settings_GyroOutputCurve_Tooltip
data.value: Reshapes the response. Linear = pass-through. Aggressive = x² (slow stays slow, fast amplifies). Relaxed = √x (slow amplifies, fast saturates). Wide / ExtraWide sit between aggressive and saturated. Composes with Acceleration.

data.name: Settings_GyroSensitivityUnits_Tooltip
data.value: Sensitivity unit display. Multiplier is the internal × scale (1 = baseline). DegPerScreenTurn is Steam-style: degrees of physical controller rotation per one full screen turn.

data.name: Settings_GyroEasyAimThreshold_Tooltip
data.value: Right-stick deflection (0–100%) below which gyro output is zeroed. 0 = always on. Steam's "gyro engaged while aiming" feel. Gyro fires only when the user pushes the right stick past the threshold.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_Subtitle
data.value: Tune how this pad's motion sensor drives mouse and stick output. Calibrate on a flat surface to zero at-rest drift, then dial in sensitivity, smoothing, and engage rules to taste.

data.name: Settings_GyroSpace_Tooltip
data.value: How gyro motion is interpreted. Local uses the raw controller axes. Player projects horizontal motion onto the real-world vertical (gravity) so the same wrist twist always turns the camera, regardless of how you hold the pad. World additionally re-projects vertical motion onto world axes.

data.name: Settings_GyroInvertPitch_Tooltip
data.value: Flips the pitch axis. Applies after the gyro space projection, independently of any per-source invert flags on the mapping table.

data.name: Settings_GyroInvertYawRoll_Tooltip
data.value: Flips the yaw axis. Also covers the roll and horizontal-blend gyro sources.

data.name: Settings_GyroRealWorldCalibration_Tooltip
data.value: In-game degrees per physical degree of controller rotation. 0 turns this off. 1.0 means a 90° wrist rotation produces a 90° camera turn. Calibrate once per game: rotate the pad a full turn and adjust until the in-game camera also rotates a full turn.

data.name: Settings_GyroTightening_Tooltip
data.value: Below this rotation rate, the input is fully replaced by the smoothing buffer's average. Drops hand tremor and microscopic drift. Default 3°/s.

data.name: Settings_GyroSmoothingThreshold_Tooltip
data.value: Above this rotation rate, the input passes through raw so fast turns retain precision. Between the tightening and smoothing thresholds, a linear ramp blends the two. Default 8°/s.

data.name: Settings_GyroSmoothingWindow_Tooltip
data.value: Length of the smoothing-buffer time window. Larger values smooth more heavily below the tightening threshold. Smaller values feel snappier. Default 50ms.

data.name: Settings_GyroAimEngageButton_Tooltip
data.value: Button that gates gyro output. Gyro fires only while this button is held. Leave unset to disable the button gate. When both this and the right-stick deflection are configured, both must be active for gyro to fire.

data.name: Settings_GyroAimEngageMode_Tooltip
data.value: Hold: gyro fires while the engage button is held. Toggle: each press flips gyro on or off, and release does nothing. Toggle is sticky across the polling tick and resets on profile switch.

data.name: Settings_GyroEngageStickSide_Tooltip
data.value: Which stick's deflection the Easy Aim threshold gates on. Right (the default) keeps existing profiles unchanged. Either gates on whichever stick moves further.

data.name: Settings_GyroEngageStickDirection_Tooltip
data.value: Which part of the engage stick the Easy Aim threshold gates on. Full (the default) uses the stick's total deflection and keeps existing profiles unchanged. X or Y gate on horizontal or vertical movement. The signed options gate on one direction only.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_Engage_Subtitle
data.value: Optional gates that limit when gyro is active. Right-stick deflection and the aim engage button can each be configured. Gyro fires only while every configured gate is active.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_ApplyToPassthrough
data.value: Apply Gyro Tuning to Motion Passthrough

data.name: Pad_Gyro_ApplyToPassthrough_Tooltip
data.value: Runs this tab's discretionary gyro tuning (deadzone, sensitivity, smoothing, response curve, invert) on the motion the virtual controller reports to the game or emulator. Turn it off to send only the calibrated reading and let the game apply its own sensitivity and smoothing. Calibration drift correction always applies either way.

data.name: Mapping_GyroSensitivity_Tooltip
data.value: Per-source gyro sensitivity multiplier. 1.0 = the engine's default (500°/s → full deflection). Values above 1.0 are more sensitive. Values below 1.0 are less sensitive.

data.name: Mapping_MouseCursorSensitivity_Tooltip
data.value: Per-source cursor sensitivity. 1.0 reaches full stick deflection at 10% of screen width from center. Values above 1.0 reach full deflection with less cursor travel. Values below 1.0 need more.

data.name: Mapping_IrPointerSensitivity_Tooltip
data.value: Per-source IR pointer sensitivity. 1.0 reaches full stick deflection at the edge of the camera's field of view. Values above 1.0 reach full deflection with less aim travel. Values below 1.0 need more.

data.name: Mapping_Sensitivity_Tooltip
data.value: Per-source sensitivity for a plain axis, slider, or gamepad stick / trigger. 1.0 leaves the input unchanged. Values above 1.0 reach full deflection with less travel. Values below 1.0 need more.

data.name: Mapping_MouseMotionSensitivity_Tooltip
data.value: Sensitivity of the mouse motion per source. 1.0 reaches full deflection at the same speed a real mouse would, values above 1.0 need less motion, values below need more.

data.name: Profiles_Description
data.value: Create per-application controller profiles that auto-switch based on the active game.

data.name: Profiles_AutoSwitch
data.value: Auto-switch profiles based on foreground application

data.name: Profiles_AutoSwitchNoRulesHint
data.value: No profile has an executable yet

data.name: Profiles_DefaultLockedHint
data.value: The built-in Default profile can't be edited or deleted.

data.name: Profiles_DeleteConfirm_Format
data.value: Delete "{0}"? Its saved slot and mapping snapshot will be destroyed.

data.name: ProfileDialog_SaveAsDescription
data.value: Snapshots every slot's mappings and per-device settings under one name. Linked executables switch to it automatically.

data.name: ProfileDialog_EditDescription
data.value: Renames the profile and updates the executables that activate it. Stored mappings and settings are unchanged.

data.name: CopyFrom_SelectDevice
data.value: Select a device to copy its settings from:

data.name: Pad_SensitivityCurveHint
data.value: Double-click chart to add point. Right-click to remove. Drag to adjust.

data.name: Pad_SensitivityCurveHintShort
data.value: Double-click to add point. Right-click to remove. Drag to adjust.

data.name: Pad_ConstantForce_Description
data.value: Apply a continuous force to this device until you toggle off. Game-driven force from any source overrides while it's active and resumes when the game stops.

data.name: Pad_ConstantForce_Position
data.value: Drag inside the grid to set direction and strength.

data.name: Pad_Sticks_Boundary_SecondLap
data.value: Covered. One more lap to refine...

data.name: Pad_Sticks_Boundary_Tooltip
data.value: Sweep the stick around its rim to map the reachable boundary, then reshape it to a full circle.

data.name: Macro_RecordHint
data.value: Press buttons or move an axis/trigger to record. Axes are detected when deflected past 50%.

data.name: Macro_AddTriggerFromList_Tooltip
data.value: Pick a trigger input from the slot's devices instead of recording it. Touchpad gestures enabled on the Touchpad tab appear here.

data.name: Pad_Either_Tooltip
data.value: When Half is on, fire on deflection past the deadzone in either direction from center (Invert has no effect).

data.name: Macro_SysVolumeHint
data.value: Continuously maps the selected axis (0–100%) to the Windows system volume, scaled to the volume limit. Use with "Always" trigger, or a button/axis trigger with "While Held" + "Until Release".

data.name: Macro_AppVolumeHint
data.value: Controls the volume of a specific application in the Windows volume mixer, scaled to the volume limit. Enter the process name (visible in Task Manager). Use with "Always" trigger, or a button/axis trigger with "While Held" + "Until Release".

data.name: Macro_MouseMoveHint
data.value: Continuously maps the selected axis to mouse movement (or scroll). Use with "Always" trigger, or a button/axis trigger with "While Held" + "Until Release". For stick-to-mouse, create two actions: one for X axis, one for Y axis.

data.name: Settings_AudioRumbleDesc
data.value: Drive controller rumble from system audio bass frequencies.

data.name: Settings_HmInactivityTimeoutTooltip
data.value: Seconds before a virtual controller is destroyed when all mapped devices are offline. 0 disables. Surviving controllers shift up to fill the gap and re-bind to lower XInput slots.

data.name: Pad_Shift_AddLayer_Tooltip
data.value: Add a shift layer. A second mapping table that activates while a button is held or toggled.

data.name: Pad_Shift_HintNameDuplicate
data.value: A layer with that name already exists on this slot.

data.name: Pad_Shift_Icon_Tooltip
data.value: Pick an emoji to show on the flyout when this layer is engaged.

data.name: Pad_Shift_DeleteConfirm_Format
data.value: Delete the "{0}" layer and all of its mapping rows? This cannot be undone.

data.name: Pad_Shift_NoInherit_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, this layer's target stays OFF instead of falling through to the Base row.

data.name: Pad_Shift_Delay_Tooltip
data.value: How long the input must stay held before the layer reacts. For Hold mode this is a debounce. For Toggle, Latch, and Sticky it makes the switch a long press: the layer flips once when the hold crosses this time, and a shorter tap does nothing. 0 reacts instantly.

data.name: Pad_Shift_CycleWrap_Tooltip
data.value: When on, stepping past the last layer returns to the first, and past the first returns to the last. When off, the cursor stops at the ends.

data.name: Pad_Shift_CycleIncludeBase_Tooltip
data.value: When on, the unshifted Base is a stop in the rotation, so cycling can land back on it. When off, the cursor stays on the checked layers and you return to Base with a separate activator.

data.name: Pad_Shift_KindButton_Subtitle
data.value: A single button (or POV direction) press engages the layer.

data.name: Pad_Shift_KindChord_Subtitle
data.value: Both buttons must be held simultaneously to engage. Cross-device chord supported.

data.name: Pad_Shift_KindAxis_Subtitle
data.value: Engages while an analog axis is past the threshold value.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeHold_Subtitle
data.value: Layer stays engaged while the activator is held. Releases when you let go.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeToggle_Subtitle
data.value: Tap to engage. Tap again to release. Layer persists across many presses.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeCustom_Subtitle
data.value: Press to latch this layer on and hold it. Press again to release back to Base. A different Latch button switches to its own layer.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeCycle_Subtitle
data.value: Each press advances through an ordered layer list. Wraps back to Base.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeSticky_Subtitle
data.value: Tap once to engage. The next mapped button press fires on the layer, then auto-releases.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModePassive_Subtitle
data.value: No button of its own. Add it to a Cycle control's queue, and the cycle reaches it.

data.name: Pad_Shift_PostponeMapping_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, the activator button still drives any row that uses it as a source. One press both changes layer AND fires the button's own mapping. When unchecked (default), the activator press is consumed by the layer change only.

data.name: Pad_Shift_InheritUnmapped_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, targets this layer doesn't explicitly map fall through to the Base layer. When unchecked (default), the layer replaces Base entirely and unmapped targets stay off.

data.name: Pad_Steering_Subtitle
data.value: Off leaves this a normal stick. The other modes make it act like a steering wheel.

data.name: Pad_MotionSteer_Subtitle
data.value: Settings for the Motion Lean input: tilt the controller like a wheel. Map "Motion Lean" to a stick axis from the input dropdown in Mappings.

data.name: Pad_FlickStick_Subtitle
data.value: Settings for the Flick Stick inputs: point the stick and the camera turns to match, sweep the rim to fine-turn. Map "Flick Stick (Right Stick)" to Mouse X from the input dropdown in Mappings, on any layer.

data.name: Settings_FlickCountsPer360_Tooltip
data.value: Mouse counts for one full 360° camera turn. Depends on the game's mouse sensitivity: raise it if a flick under-rotates, lower it if it over-rotates.

data.name: Settings_FlickTime_Tooltip
data.value: How long a full 180° flick takes to complete, with an ease-out. Shorter turns finish in the same time.

data.name: Settings_FlickThreshold_Tooltip
data.value: Stick deflection that starts a flick, as a fraction of full deflection. While flicking, the release point drops to 90% of this.

data.name: Settings_FlickSnapMode_Tooltip
data.value: Snap the flick to fixed angles for more consistent turns. Forward Only snaps every flick to dead ahead.

data.name: Settings_FlickSnapStrength_Tooltip
data.value: How strongly a flick pulls toward the snapped angle. 1 snaps fully, 0 disables snapping, values between blend.

data.name: Settings_FlickForwardDeadzone_Tooltip
data.value: A flick within this angle of dead ahead turns nothing. Lets you start a sweep without a flick-turn.

data.name: Settings_FlickSmoothing_Tooltip
data.value: Smooths rim-sweep noise. -1 uses the automatic tiered window, 0 turns smoothing off, larger values smooth bigger per-tick rotations.

data.name: Settings_FlickOnEngage_Tooltip
data.value: When the layer hosting Flick Stick engages with the stick already deflected, fire the flick immediately. Off keeps the camera still and tracks rotation from the current stick angle.

data.name: Pad_Steering_LockFeedback_Subtitle
data.value: When a stick set to a steering mode is turned all the way to full lock, play a cue (rumble, trigger, or lightbar) so you feel the limit. All off by default.

data.name: Pad_Wheel_Subtitle
data.value: Steering range, auto centering, and shift lights for force feedback wheels.

data.name: Pad_Steering_Lock_PaletteEmpty
data.value: Add colors to step through, one per lock.

data.name: Pad_Pointer_Subtitle
data.value: Aim this Wii Remote at the screen with its IR camera. Needs a sensor bar, or two infrared LEDs, above or below the display.

data.name: Pad_Pointer_Mode_Tooltip
data.value: How the aim drives the OS cursor. Mouse points absolutely. FPS Mouse turns the offset from screen center into smooth cursor velocity. The border modes confine the cursor to a 4:3 or 16:9 region and pin it to the border while you aim outside it.

data.name: Pad_Pointer_FpsSpeed_Tooltip
data.value: Cursor speed at full deflection. 35 matches the Touchmote-lineage default.

data.name: Pad_Pointer_ModeNote
data.value: Modes shape the cursor only. IR Pointer X/Y mapped to sticks or buttons keeps reading the raw aim.

data.name: MacroAction_PointerModeCycle_Tooltip
data.value: Advances the Wii pointer mode through the modes selected below for every IR-capable remote on the slot. Each fire moves to the next checked mode. The cycle position is per-action and resets on app restart.

data.name: Macro_PointerCycleModes_Hint
data.value: Pick which pointer modes the macro should cycle through. Each fire advances to the next checked mode.

data.name: Pad_Audio_Subtitle
data.value: Macro sounds and mirrored system audio play through the selected controller’s built-in speaker, over USB or Bluetooth. Pick the device in the dropdown above. Every setting here follows it.

data.name: Pad_Audio_Output_Desc
data.value: Sounds route to the selected controller automatically. Over USB the pad’s own audio endpoint is matched by hardware container. Over Bluetooth the audio is streamed in Sony HID frames.

data.name: Pad_Audio_MirrorSource_Tooltip
data.value: Which playback device to mirror to the controller speaker. Games that send specific sounds to a separate playback device can target this one.

data.name: Pad_Audio_Test_Tooltip
data.value: Play a short beep on the selected output device

data.name: Pad_Audio_Macros_Desc
data.value: Sounds are played by macros: a trigger (button press, release, hold, or formula) plus a Play Sound action. Build them here or on the Macros tab. Delays, repeats, and toggles all work.

data.name: Pad_Audio_NoSoundMacros
data.value: No sound macros yet. Create one and pick a sound file and a trigger.

data.name: Pad_Audio_OpenMacro_Tooltip
data.value: Open this macro on the Macros tab

data.name: MacroAction_PlaySound_Tooltip
data.value: Play a sound file (.wav, .mp3, .m4a, .aac, .wma, .flac) on this pad’s output device

data.name: MacroAction_SoundStop_Tooltip
data.value: Stops every macro sound on this pad. Pair with a looping Play Sound to end it from another macro.

data.name: Macro_Sound_Loop_Tooltip
data.value: Repeat the sound until a Stop Sounds action runs, or for While Held / Until Released macros, until the trigger is released

data.name: Pad_Audio_Mirror
data.value: Mirror system audio to the controller speaker

data.name: Pad_Audio_Engage_Tooltip
data.value: When the mirrored audio plays as haptic tones. Gate it on a held input or on game rumble so music does not buzz the controller all the time.

data.name: Pad_Audio_EngageRelease_Tooltip
data.value: How long the mirror keeps playing after the engage source drops, so the tone does not clip off instantly.

data.name: Pad_Audio_ToneFilter_Tooltip
data.value: What happens to tones above the limit. High-pitched beeps can be cut off, or folded down an octave at a time so they keep their character at a lower pitch. Folding is recommended. Applies to mirrored audio, macro sounds, and the test tone.

data.name: Pad_Audio_ToneLimit_Tooltip
data.value: Tones above this frequency are cut or folded. The default 800 Hz keeps engine and impact rumble while catching high-pitched beeps.

data.name: Pad_Audio_Mirror_Tooltip
data.value: Copies whatever the system default output plays to this controller’s built-in speaker, in parallel. Works over USB and Bluetooth.

data.name: Pad_Audio_NoSpeaker
data.value: The selected device has no built-in speaker. Macro sounds for this pad play on the system default output.

data.name: Pad_Audio_Reset_All
data.value: Reset every Sound Output setting for this device to defaults

data.name: About_NAudioDesc
data.value: WASAPI loopback capture for the controller-audio mirror and the audio-bass trigger rumble. By Mark Heath. MIT.

data.name: About_BouncyCastleDesc
data.value: Cryptography for Remote Link pairing and transport (X25519, Ed25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305). Bouncy Castle Licence, an MIT-style license.

data.name: About_BthPS3Desc
data.value: Bundled Bluetooth profile and PSM filter drivers by nefarius that let a DualShock 3 connect over the shared radio. Installed in-app at pairing time. BSD 3-Clause.

data.name: About_DsHidMiniDesc
data.value: DualShock 3 protocol reference by Benjamin Höglinger-Stelzer: sixpair feature reports, Bluetooth output-report template, enable ordering, battery map. PadForge's implementation is original C#. BSD 3-Clause.

data.name: About_NefariusDevMgmtDesc
data.value: Driver-store install, Bluetooth class filter registration, and USB port cycling for the in-app BthPS3 setup, by nefarius. MIT.

data.name: About_LibusbDesc
data.value: USB access for the Switch 2 Pro wired driver, shipped as libusb-1.0.dll. LGPL-2.1.

data.name: About_NipplejsDesc
data.value: Touch joystick in the phone Web Controller, by Yoann Moinet. MIT.

data.name: About_GameControllerDbDesc
data.value: Community gamepad mapping database PadForge's bundled mappings extend. zlib.

data.name: About_XbledctlDesc
data.value: Xbox Guide button LED research: the XboxGIP packet layout and discovery sequence, by Leclowndu93150. MIT.

data.name: About_JoyShockMapperDesc
data.value: Winding-angle steering and lean math, by JibbSmart and Electronicks. MIT.

data.name: About_GamepadMotionHelpersDesc
data.value: Player-space and world-space gyro conversion, by JibbSmart. MIT.

data.name: About_SteamControllerSingerDesc
data.value: Steam Controller (2015) haptic report layout and note-period math, by Pila and Roboron3042. BSD 3-Clause.

data.name: About_SteamHapticsSingerDesc
data.value: Steam Controller 2026 and Steam Deck LFO-tone haptic layout, by Pila, Crazy, and AAGaming. BSD 3-Clause.

data.name: About_HitboxerDesc
data.value: SOCD cleaning semantics for the Snap Tap modes, by valignatev. MIT.

data.name: About_SteamKit2Desc
data.value: Steam network client that fetches Steam Workshop controller configs over an anonymous session, by Ryan Stecker and the SteamRE Team. LGPL-2.1.

data.name: About_ProtobufNetDesc
data.value: Protocol Buffers serializer SteamKit2 uses for the Steam wire protocol, by Marc Gravell. Apache-2.0.

data.name: About_ZstdSharpDesc
data.value: Zstandard decompression SteamKit2 uses for Steam depot chunks, a C# port of the zstd library by Oleg Stepanischev. MIT.

data.name: About_DolphinDesc
data.value: Wii pairing ceremony and speaker ADPCM documentation. GPL, read as documentation only, no GPL code ships.

data.name: About_Ds4WindowsDesc
data.value: DualShock behavior documentation: idle disconnect, touchpad boundaries, battery decode. GPL, documentation only.

data.name: About_XoneXowDesc
data.value: GIP LED command documentation corroborating xbledctl. GPL, documentation only.

data.name: About_WiimoteLibDesc
data.value: Wii IR camera and Balance Board behavior documentation, by Brian Peek. Ms-PL.

data.name: About_JoyconSingerDesc
data.value: Joy-Con HD rumble wire-format documentation, by Sergey004. Read for protocol facts only.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_Desc
data.value: Hold the gesture button, flick, and one action fires when you release: left, right, up, down, or a plain click below the flick distance. Map the five gestures on the Mappings tab or use them as macro triggers.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_Enabled_Tooltip
data.value: Arms the gesture recognizer for this mouse on this slot. The gesture button keeps its normal click while gesturing, so pick a side button you do not otherwise map.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_Button_Tooltip
data.value: The mouse buttons that arm the recognizer while held. Each selected button carries its own five gestures, so different buttons can drive different actions.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_FlickThreshold_Tooltip
data.value: Net movement the flick must reach by release to count as a direction. Below it, the release fires the Click gesture.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_Custom_Tooltip
data.value: Arms the recognizer with a recorded input from any device instead of a mouse button: a key, a gamepad button, or an analog input such as a pedal. Record the input below.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_CustomInput_Tooltip
data.value: The input that arms the Custom gesture session while held, recorded from any device on this slot. Buttons and keys arm while pressed. Analog inputs such as a pedal arm past half travel.

data.name: MacroAction_PointerModeSet_Tooltip
data.value: Sets the Wii pointer mode to the one selected below for every IR-capable remote on the slot.

data.name: Macro_PointerSetMode_Hint
data.value: Pick the pointer mode this action applies.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_GuideLed_Subtitle
data.value: Brightness of the glowing Guide or Home button. Xbox One and later controllers accept it over USB. The 2015 Steam Controller accepts it on any connection, and all Steam Controllers share one brightness. Switch Pro Controllers and right Joy-Cons (alone, paired, or in the charging grip) accept it on any connection.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_GuideLed_Mode_Tooltip
data.value: Device Default leaves the LED exactly as the controller firmware set it. Fixed Brightness holds the level below. Battery Level makes a fuller battery brighter and never drops below 10%. Xbox controllers accept Guide LED commands over USB only, so this setting has no effect on a Bluetooth connection. Switch controllers accept Home LED commands on any connection.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_GuideLed_Brightness_Tooltip
data.value: Guide button LED brightness from 0% (off) to 100% (full). Applies while the mode is Fixed Brightness.

data.name: MacroAction_GuideLedBrightness_Tooltip
data.value: Sets the Guide or Home button LED brightness for every capable controller on the slot. Xbox controllers accept it over USB only.

data.name: Macro_GuideLedBrightness_Hint
data.value: Applies to Xbox controllers over USB, the 2015 Steam Controller, and Switch controllers with a Home button LED. Pair two of these actions to flash the LED when a macro starts and restore it when it ends.

data.name: Pad_Combine_StickTrim_Description
data.value: The row's last source is a trim stick. While the other sources hold the trigger, pushing the stick up raises the held level and pulling it down lowers it. Built for fine throttle and brake control on pads without analog triggers.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_TrimDeadzone_Tooltip
data.value: Stick deflection below this percentage is ignored, so steering with the same stick never nudges the held trigger level. Only the stick's stronger vertical pushes adjust it.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_TrimRate_Tooltip
data.value: How fast a fully deflected stick slides the held level, in percent of the trigger range per second. 100 sweeps from empty to full in one second.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_TrimReset_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, releasing the trigger snaps the held level back to 100% so the next press starts full. Unchecked keeps the trimmed level across releases until you adjust it again.

data.name: Pad_Shift_AutoCancel_Tooltip
data.value: While the layer is toggled on, it switches itself back off after this many milliseconds with none of the layer's own mapped inputs active. The timer starts when the layer engages and restarts on every layer input. 0 keeps the layer on until you toggle it off yourself.

data.name: Pad_ResetTrimRate
data.value: Reset the trim speed to 100% per second.

data.name: Pad_ResetTrimResetOnRelease
data.value: Reset to snapping the level back to 100% on release.

data.name: Pad_ResetShiftAutoCancel
data.value: Reset auto-cancel to 0 (the layer stays on until toggled off).

data.name: Pad_ResetShiftDelay
data.value: Reset the delay to 0 (the layer reacts instantly).

data.value: Browse community-made Steam Input controller configurations and translate them into PadForge profiles. PadForge connects directly to Steam (store.steampowered.com, api.steampowered.com, steamcommunity.com, cdn.steamusercontent.com, cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com, avatars.fastly.steamstatic.com) only when you search and when you open a config. Your search text and the chosen config are the only data sent. No telemetry, no third-party service, no Steam sign-in.

data.name: Macro_HoldForMs_Tooltip
data.value: Fires once after the trigger has been held continuously for the hold time. A shorter tap does nothing.

data.name: Macro_DoublePress_Tooltip
data.value: Fires when the trigger is pressed twice within the press window. If held on the second press, it stays active until release.

data.name: Macro_SinglePress_Tooltip
data.value: Fires when a press is not followed by a second press within the press window, so it can share a button with Double or Triple Press. On Press fires instantly instead.

data.name: Macro_TriplePress_Tooltip
data.value: Fires when the trigger is pressed three times within the press window. If held on the third press, it stays active until release.

data.name: Macro_Toggle_Tooltip
data.value: First press latches the actions on. Press again to release. Holds and repeats stay active until the second press.

data.name: Macro_Turbo_Tooltip
data.value: Repeats the actions at the interval below for as long as the trigger is held.

data.name: Macro_ToggleInterval_Tooltip
data.value: While latched, the actions repeat at this interval.

data.name: MacroAction_RepeatVcButtonWhileHeld_Tooltip
data.value: Pulses the controller button on and off at the interval for as long as the trigger is held (autofire / turbo).

data.name: MacroAction_ToggleVcButton_Tooltip
data.value: Each fire latches or unlatches the controller button. A latched button stays held until the next fire or until the macro is disabled.

data.name: MacroAction_ToggleKey_Tooltip
data.value: Each fire latches or unlatches the key. A latched key stays held down until the next fire or until the macro is disabled.

data.name: MacroAction_AxisHold_Tooltip
data.value: Writes the axis value every frame for the duration. With repeat Until Release the axis stays asserted until the trigger releases.

data.name: MacroAction_MouseWheelTap_Tooltip
data.value: Sends one discrete mouse wheel detent per fire. The value is the signed tick count (positive scrolls up or right).

data.name: MacroAction_MouseNudge_Tooltip
data.value: Moves the mouse cursor by a fixed number of pixels per fire. Positive X moves right, positive Y moves down; negative values are allowed.

data.name: MacroAction_CycleTapList_Tooltip
data.value: Each fire performs the next tap in the step list and advances. With wrap enabled the list restarts after the last step; without it, firing stops at the end.

data.name: MacroAction_ToggleMouseButton_Tooltip
data.value: Each fire latches or unlatches the mouse button. A latched button stays held down until the next fire or until the macro is disabled.

data.name: MacroAction_ToggleVcAxis_Tooltip
data.value: Each fire latches or unlatches the axis value. While latched the axis is written every frame until the next fire or until the macro is disabled.

data.name: MacroAction_RepeatVcAxisWhileHeld_Tooltip
data.value: While the trigger is held, asserts the axis value on an on/off square wave with the set interval.

data.name: MacroAction_ToggleWheel_Tooltip
data.value: Each fire latches or unlatches a continuous scroll. While latched, sends the tick count once per interval until the next fire or until the macro is disabled.

data.name: MacroAction_ToggleWheel_Format
data.value: Toggle wheel scroll ({0} ticks every {1} ms)

data.name: Macro_PulseWhileLatched_Tooltip
data.value: While latched, pulse the output on and off at the repeat interval instead of holding it solid.

data.name: MacroAction_AxisAdd_Tooltip
data.value: Adds the signed value on top of what the mapping already wrote to the axis, every frame for the duration. Negative values subtract. Trigger targets add on the pull scale (100% = full pull).

data.name: MacroAction_AxisSetLatched_Tooltip
data.value: Holds the axis at the value until released, surviving combo breaks. Firing another latched step on the same axis replaces the value, so steps separated by Combo Breaks build a press-by-press ladder. Release Axis Latches returns the axis to physical control.

data.name: MacroAction_AxisLatchRelease_Tooltip
data.value: Clears latched axis values (latched steps and axis toggles) for the chosen axis, or all axes, across every macro on this slot, returning the axis to physical control.

data.name: MacroAction_AxisScale_Tooltip
data.value: Multiplies the axis’s current value while active: -50% halves the deflection (run becomes walk), +50% amplifies half again, clamped to full scale. Composes with the physical input, so no yield is needed.

data.name: MacroAction_ComboBreak_Tooltip
data.value: The combo pauses here. Press the trigger again to continue. A held trigger must be released first.

data.name: Macro_AxisYieldToPhysical_Tooltip
data.value: When physical movement pushes the target past the threshold, the macro stops writing the axis for the rest of the activation.

data.name: MacroAction_GyroRecenter_Tooltip
data.value: Zeroes the pad's accumulated gyro aim references on press. Smoothing history clears, the Motion Lean neutral re-captures, and the gravity estimate re-seeds from the controller's current pose.

data.name: Menu_EmptyHint
data.value: Menus turn a physical stick or touchpad into an on-screen ring or grid. Add a menu, pick what opens it, then label each cell and give it a binding.

data.name: Menu_Style_Tip
data.value: Radial Ring picks a cell by direction, like a weapon wheel. Touch Grid picks a cell by position: where the finger sits on the pad, or where the stick points.

data.name: Menu_HostInput_Tip
data.value: The input that opens and steers this menu, read from the slot's assigned physical controllers. A stick opens it when pushed past the Engage Deadzone. A touchpad opens it on touch.

data.name: Menu_HostHalf_Tip
data.value: Limit this menu to one half of the trackpad, so two menus can share the pad.

data.name: Menu_FireMode_Tip
data.value: When the highlighted cell fires its binding. Each choice is explained below.

data.name: Menu_Fire_Click_Desc
data.value: Fires while the stick or trackpad is clicked in: point at the cell, then press the stick down (stick click) or click the trackpad. The binding is held until the click releases.

data.name: Menu_Fire_ClickRelease_Desc
data.value: Fires once when the click releases: point at the cell, click the stick or trackpad in, then let the click go.

data.name: Menu_Fire_TouchRelease_Desc
data.value: Fires once when you let go: lift your finger off the pad, or let the stick snap back to center while a cell is highlighted.

data.name: Menu_Fire_Always_Desc
data.value: The binding is held the whole time the cell is highlighted. No click needed.

data.name: Menu_Cells_Tip
data.value: How many cells the menu has. For a radial ring this counts the ring only; the center cell is separate.

data.name: Menu_HasCenter_Tip
data.value: Adds a center cell, selected while the stick or finger rests inside the Engage Deadzone.

data.name: Menu_Deadzone_Tip
data.value: For sticks, how far to push before the menu opens and ring cells highlight. On radial menus it is also the center region for both sticks and touchpads: inside it, the center cell is selected when one exists.

data.name: Menu_ShowLabels_Tip
data.value: Draw each cell's label on the on-screen overlay.

data.name: Menu_Position_Tip
data.value: Where the overlay's center sits on screen, in percent. 50 and 50 is the middle.

data.name: Menu_Scale_Tip
data.value: Overlay size, in percent of its normal size.

data.name: Menu_CellLabel_Tip
data.value: Text shown on this cell in the overlay.

data.name: Menu_BindingKind_Tip
data.value: What this cell does when it fires: "Keyboard Key" presses a keyboard key, "Controller Button" presses a button on this slot's virtual controller. A cell set to "None" still fires as a menu-item source for Mappings rows and macro triggers.

data.name: Menu_HostInput_Caption
data.value: Read from the physical controllers assigned to this slot, not from the virtual controller's layout. The cell bindings below are what the menu outputs.

data.name: Menu_CustomAxis_Tip
data.value: Record any two axes to steer the menu: push past the Engage Deadzone to open it. This is how joysticks, wheels, and other non-gamepad devices host menus.

data.name: Menu_ClickInput_Tip
data.value: The button the On Click and On Click Release fire modes use, recordable from any assigned device. Empty keeps the host's default: the stick click or the trackpad click. Custom Axes openers have no default, so record one to use those fire modes.

data.name: Dashboard_MenuOverlayDescription
data.value: Show the on-screen ring or grid while a radial or touch menu is engaged. Menus still fire with the overlay off.

data.name: Workshop_Tr_MenuIconUnresolved
data.value: menu cell icon not recognized ({0}), so the cell keeps its text label

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Subtitle
data.value: Routes the game rumble and force feedback this virtual controller receives to an audio output as low-frequency tones for bass shakers and subwoofers.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Card_Desc
data.value: Works with Xbox, DualShock 4 / DualSense, and Nintendo Switch Pro virtual controllers, plus Extended virtual controllers with force feedback, such as racing wheels. Only game feedback plays through the audio output. Macro and test rumble stay on the controller.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Enable
data.value: Route rumble to an audio output

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Enable_Tooltip
data.value: Plays the game rumble and force feedback this virtual controller receives as low-frequency tones on the selected audio output. Turning it off keeps every setting.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_OutputDevice_Tooltip
data.value: The playback device that receives the rumble tones. System default follows the Windows default playback device. If the selected device disappears, audio stays off until it returns.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Status_Missing
data.value: The selected output device is unavailable. Audio stays off until it returns.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_BluetoothHint
data.value: Bluetooth audio devices add noticeable latency.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_ChannelMode_Tooltip
data.value: Mono plays every voice on all speaker channels. Controller Stereo splits them like the controller: low motor and left trigger on the left channel, high motor and right trigger on the right.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_MasterGain_Tooltip
data.value: Overall loudness applied after each voice's own gain. Keep headroom so the four voices do not clip when they play together.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_VoiceEnable_Tooltip
data.value: Plays this feedback channel as a tone. Gain and frequency stay set while it is off.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Frequency_Tooltip
data.value: Tone frequency for this channel, 20 to 120 Hz. Run the frequency sweep to find where your shaker responds strongest.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Gain_Tooltip
data.value: Loudness of this channel before master gain.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Test_Tooltip
data.value: Plays this channel's tone for 1.5 seconds at its set gain.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Sweep_Tooltip
data.value: Sweeps a tone from 20 to 120 Hz over eight seconds on the low motor routing. Note where your shaker responds strongest and set the voice frequencies there.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_StopTest_Tooltip
data.value: Stops the test tone or sweep.

data.name: Nfc_WaitingController
data.value: Tap a tag on your Switch controller…
